details:
This package is a fork of the Baileys WhatsApp Web library (npm) and belongs to the "PhantomSub" family described by OX Security in September 2026: the publisher injected code that, without the installer asking, uses the installer's own authenticated WhatsApp session to follow WhatsApp Channels (newsletters) the publisher chose.

`package/src/Socket/messages-recv.js` line 37 defines a character-code decoder (`qvnr`). Lines 39-47 use it to build two channel identifiers (`120363428355171197@newsletter` and `120363428984357510@newsletter`) and the method names `newsletterFollow` and `newsletterMute`, so none of them appears in the source as text.

Lines 1744-1757: 30 seconds after the connection opens, the library follows each channel and, 3 seconds later, mutes it, so the user is not notified of its posts.

`package/src/Socket/newsletter.js` lines 167-193 also download a channel list from a file on raw.githubusercontent.com (`noxXza/data/refs/heads/main/noxleys.json`) 30 seconds after the connection opens, and follow every channel in it. The publisher can change that list without publishing a new version. I did not fetch it.

The README does not mention it. The repository field names `Verucaa/vp-baileys`.

`@nerxa/socketon` 1.21.2 and `xdc-baileys` 1.22.4 ship byte-identical copies of both files.

Line numbers refer to version 9.0.34.

Static review of the published tarball found no code that sends WhatsApp credentials or session keys off-host, no install-time payload (the only install hook, where present, is Baileys' stock Node.js version check in `engine-requirements.js`), and no persistence; the payload runs when an application creates a WhatsApp socket with the library. The harm is the covert use of the victim's account to inflate the publisher's channel followers.

SHA-256 of the published npm tarball: 9.0.34: `0065869aa3f0b0d38acf6322a0d447bada8d44416e44d69511727a2af10eff80`.
